newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas gets Vietnam nod for Dai Hung project.
newsitem.headline: Petronas gets Vietnam nod for Dai Hung project.

text.p: Malaysia's national oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said on Monday it has received approval from the Vietnamese government to take up stake in the Dai Hung oilfield project.
"We have received approval from Vietnamese authorities on the Dai Hung project and effectively we are the operator of Dai Hung," Petronas president and chief executive officer Hassan Marican said.
He said Petronas had taken up the shares of Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) and that they had not acquired the shares amounting to 63.5 percent of Dai Hung's equity.
The Dai Hung field was originally estimated to hold 800 million barrels of crude but the estimates have gradually fallen to 100 million barrels.
BHP last week said the government of Vietnam had granted formal approval of BHP's assignment of its 43.75 percent interest in the Dai Hung project to Petronas.
With the assignment, Petronas now holds a 63.5 percent stake in the oil field.

The assignment of the stake in the offshore oil project, which is effective from December 1, 1996, came after disappointment at lower than expected reserves and regulatory problems with the Vietnamese government.
